component.name: Pereprava
component.summary: Dashboard for rclone/rsync backup jobs run via systemd --user

description.p: Pereprava is a GTK4/libadwaita dashboard for rclone/rsync backup jobs run as systemd --user timers, plus persistent rclone mount points run as systemd --user services. See all your jobs at a glance — last run, next run, mounted/unmounted, success/failure — and create or edit them through a form instead of hand-writing systemd units.

Non-destructive rclone copy is the default job type. Anything that can delete files at its destination (rclone sync, rclone bisync, rsync --delete, or a custom command) is flagged loudly in the UI and requires an explicit acknowledgment before it can be saved.

ul.li: Job types: rclone copy/sync/bisync, rclone check, rsync, a persistent rclone mount, or a custom command
Include/exclude glob filtering, bandwidth limiting with time-of-day schedules, and pre/post-run hook commands
Conditional scheduling — only run on AC power, or only on a specific Wi-Fi network
Duplicate and Restore actions, per-job run history, and live transfer progress for rclone jobs
Guided remote setup for pCloud (OAuth) and client-side encrypted remotes
Desktop notifications the moment a job or mount transitions into a failed state
Export/import job definitions, and an optional system tray icon reflecting overall job health

description.p: Pereprava manages real systemd --user units and reads whatever host paths your jobs point at, so the flatpak build talks to systemd, rclone, rsync, and systemd-analyze on the host (via the Flatpak portal) rather than trying to bundle its own copies — your jobs, logs, and existing units are exactly the same ones a non-flatpak install would see.

screenshot.caption: Job list showing last run, next run, and status for scheduled backups and mounts

description.p: "True Reading" — fixes a stuck "Skipped — a Run Condition isn't met" status.

ul.li: A job no longer shows a Run Condition skip after its AC-power/Wi-Fi condition has been removed (or was never set). The status display could get stuck on a stale skip from before the condition was edited away, since systemd's own condition-result tracking only refreshes on the unit's next actual start.

Pereprava is now available as a flatpak alongside the existing install script. It still manages real systemd --user units and calls systemctl/rclone/rsync/systemd-analyze/loginctl on the host rather than bundling its own copies, so an existing non-flatpak install's jobs are picked up unchanged.
New app icon, installed for both distributions.

description.p: "Common Ground" — reliability fixes for invisible failures.

ul.li: rclone/rsync are resolved via PATH and common install locations instead of being hardcoded to /usr/bin.
A job skipped by an unmet Run Condition is now correctly classified as skipped, not a failure.
The Add/Edit form's dry-run "Test" correctly restores the "no changes" message for a genuinely no-op preview.

description.p: "Open Passage" — fixed the needs-repair dead end, and gave a stuck discrepancy row Edit/Delete actions.

"Still Waters" — the app now keeps monitoring in the background when the window is closed, with an optional system tray icon reflecting overall job health, and a mount-point fix for a stray KDE metadata file that could trip rclone's empty-destination safety check.
"Steady Current" — live transfer progress for rclone jobs via an opt-in loopback control API, shown as a real percent/speed/ETA instead of just "Running…".

"Third Crossing" — rclone check, bandwidth limits, include/exclude filters, pre/post-run hooks, conditional scheduling, job duplication, one-click restore, per-job run history, guided encrypted-remote setup, and remote quota display.
"Second Crossing" — dry-run testing, export/import, failure notifications, remote validation, and guided pCloud setup.
"Anchor" — added the rclone mount job type.
"First Crossing" — initial release: log-file picker, uninstall script, changelog polish.
